literal: If desiring to be attained, let one renounce; after renouncing, here, things that naturally belong are many.
translation: If one desires the state of supreme joy to be attained, let them renounce. After renouncing, many are the joys that naturally follow in this very state.
modern: ஒருவர் இன்பம் உண்டாக விரும்பினால் பற்றுகளைத் துறக்க வேண்டும்; அவ்வாறு துறந்த பிறகு, இவ்வுலகிலேயே அவருக்கு இயற்கையாகவே வந்து சேரும் நன்மைகள் பலவாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the immediate and spontaneous rewards of renunciation. If a person desires true, lasting happiness to arise, the path is to renounce worldly attachments. Once they have renounced, they do not experience a void; instead, many natural joys and benefits ('இயற்பால') spontaneously flow to them in this very life ('ஈண்டு'). The poet shows that true freedom brings an abundance of peace that cannot be acquired through possession.
